newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firm, light sweet indications higher.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firm, light sweet indications higher.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were firm on Wednesday with indications the light sweet market was rising further.
A producer sold 600,000 barrels of early November Kutubu to a major at higher than the previous deal done, which was at Tapis quotes plus 18 cents.
The firmer tone was reflected in the paper Tapis market, the regional benchmark for light sweet grades, which firmed 30 cents on the day to $23.35/$23.50 per barrel from a day earlier.
However, this was largely supported by the firmer futures markets in the wake of a fall in API distillate stocks.
November Brent in London was up 31 cents on the day at $23.38 per barrel.

Medium grades were also looking firmer with traders saying 300,000 barrels of early November Bontang Mix was traded to a major from a U.S. producer at ICP plus 10 cents, firmer than recent deals said done around ICP flat or a small discount.
Traders said Qatar's new crude, Al Rayyan, traded into Japan at a price of Arab Heavy less 50 cents.
A November Masila was also traded between a producer and a U.S. major on the unusual basis of MPM plus 10 cents. The deal was not confirmed by late trading.
Traders estimated there were four or five cargos of November Dubai left to sell into safe hands, one Murban and one Lower Zakum.
Several Oman's were still on the November shelf, but traders were not surprised owing to the uncertainty over the MPM.
The uncertainty was making offering into the Bangchak tender difficult because Oman is scheduled to release its September MPM anytime this week.
But traders were likely to offer into the tender on the basis of Dubai prices to avoid exposure to the MPM.
